answer: Starting low-dose aspirin (baby aspirin) at 12-28 weeks of gestation is recommended for high-risk pregnant patients to reduce the risk of preeclampsia [ACOG, 2020]. This guidance applies specifically to women at high risk of developing preeclampsia. Aspirin is not routinely recommended for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease in non-pregnant adults, except in select cases after a risk-benefit discussion with a clinician [ACC/AHA, 2019].

results.content: Low-dose aspirin starting at 12-28 weeks of gestation is recommended for patients at high risk of preeclampsia. Magnesium sulfate is recommended for seizure prophylaxis in patients with severe features of preeclampsia.

Aspirin for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease is not routinely recommended due to bleeding risk, except in select high-risk adults 40-70 years after a risk-benefit discussion with their clinician.
